context: Tests whether the agent uses git mv for file renames (to preserve history), produces a clean non-WIP commit, and follows correct commit message format for a refactor/chore type change.

checklist.name: git mv in rename script
checklist.description: rename.sh contains 'git mv' commands (not 'mv' followed by 'git add', and not 'cp'+'rm')

checklist.name: All three renames covered
checklist.description: rename.sh includes git mv commands covering all three files: StringHelpers.js, DateHelpers.js, and APIHelpers.js

checklist.name: Correct commit type
checklist.description: The rename commit header uses 'refactor' or 'chore' as the type — not 'fix' or 'feat'

checklist.name: Commit header format
checklist.description: The rename commit header follows type(scope): description format with imperative mood and lowercase description start

checklist.name: No trailing period
checklist.description: The commit header does NOT end with a period

checklist.name: Header 72-char limit
checklist.description: The commit header is at most 72 characters

checklist.name: No WIP commit
checklist.description: git-log.txt does NOT contain a commit with 'WIP', 'wip', 'temp', or 'tmp' in the header

checklist.name: rename.sh exists
checklist.description: A file named rename.sh is present in the workspace

checklist.name: git-log.txt exists
checklist.description: A file named git-log.txt is present in the workspace with at least one commit entry

checklist.name: Specific file staging
checklist.description: rename.sh does NOT use 'git add .' or 'git add -A' — files are staged individually or via git mv which handles staging automatically
